candidates.title: Walk fast but be careful: Understanding Parallel Sampling in Masked Diffusion
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we use random walks on graphs as a verifiable sandbox for studying parallel sampling strategies in masked diffusion models (MDMs). We train an MDM on random walk samples from a fixed graph. The graph and transition kernel are never shown to the model and serve as latent structure that is both controllable and enables evaluation. The framework provides a validity check for generated walks and a measure of distributional fidelity through the estimated transition kernel. Using simple graphs, we theoretically prove that parallel unmasking via widely used scores such as lowest entropy is not uniformly better than random parallel sampling; even with exact conditional probabilities, performance critically depends on the conditional dependence structure induced by the graph, a phenomenon difficult to isolate in benchmarks like Sudoku. We also develop training-free bisection samplers for MDMs, which take logarithmically many steps in the sequence length and are provably exact for random walks if the learned marginals are exact. Experiments on graph-walk tasks confirm that different parallel samplers perform better on different graph structures. Experiments on pretrained MDMs show that bisection-style samplers provide strong speed-quality tradeoffs on OpenWebText generation and reasoning benchmarks including GSM8K, MBPP, and HumanEval. Together, these results use graph walks to uncover conditional dependence as a key principle of parallel MDM sampling and translate this insight into efficient samplers that transfer to language generation and reasoning.
candidates.reason: マスク拡散モデルの並列サンプリングを解析し、学習不要な二分法サンプラーを提案して系列長に対して対数ステップで生成できることを示し、事前学習済みMDMの言語生成と推論ベンチマークで速度と品質のトレードオフ改善を実証するデコード手法である。
